title: Add JSON Schema response_format with strict validation, structured errors, and OpenAI compatibility mapping
author: Marina Alvarez
description: Motivation: Add first-class support for a JSON Schema-based response_format to enable structured outputs with server-side validation and a strict mode that rejects non-conforming outputs. This PR implements: 1) a new response_format variant (type: "json_schema") accepted by the Redwood API and OpenAI-compat layer; 2) server-side validation against the provided schema with detailed structured error messages; 3) a "strict" flag which, when true, causes the generation to fail with a validation error instead of returning a best-effort response; 4) streaming compatibility so that partial streaming tokens are emitted while validation is performed incrementally and a final validation step runs at generation end; 5) mapping rules in the openai compatibility shim to translate the OpenAI-style response_format to Redwood internal handlers; 6) SDK surface updates (Python + TS) to expose the new response_format shape and helper utilities to construct simple schemas; 7) docs and release notes. Behavior summary: - Request shape: response_format:{"type":"json_schema","schema":<JSON Schema JSON>,"strict":true|false,"on_validation_fail":"error|best_effort"} - When strict=true (default for this PR is strict=false to avoid breaking apps), server validates final structured output. If validation fails and on_validation_fail="error" then the API returns a 400 with a documented validation payload; when on_validation_fail="best_effort" the server attempts minimal repairs (trimming extra fields, coercion when safe) and returns the structured result plus a "validation_warnings" array. - Streaming: streaming tokens are emitted as before; we buffer a lightweight canonical JSON reconstruction for validation. Final validation happens on generation end; if strict mode triggers an error, we send a terminal error event in the stream and close the stream with an error code. - OpenAI compat: added mapping so OpenAI requests using response_format:{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":...} are normalized to Redwood schema field names and options. Implementation notes: - Core API: added response_format parser and validator in server/api/response_format.go; validation uses our existing schema-utils with additional type coercion rules and clear diagnostics. - Streaming runtime: minimal additional memory used to keep a string builder per request; incremental validation checks for early fatal conditions (e.g., invalid top-level type) to fail fast. - SDKs: python client adds ResponseFormat.json_schema helper; typescript client adds types and small runtime helper. - Tests: unit tests for validator, integration tests exercising streaming + strict=true, and OpenAI compatibility mapping tests. - Docs: detailed examples added to redwood-docs with examples of strict vs best_effort, sample error payloads, and guidance for constructing robust schemas. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is non-strict and will not break existing customers. Migration guidance provided in docs. Checklist: - [x] API handler and parser - [x] Schema validator + diagnostic payloads - [x] Streaming behavior + terminal stream error events - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping - [x] Python + TS SDK surface updates - [x] Tests (unit + integration) - [x] Docs and release notes
commits: feat(api): add response_format json_schema parser and validation hooks
feat(runtime): integrate incremental validation into streaming runtime
chore(sdk/ts): expose types for json_schema response_format
test: add unit/integration tests for strict and best_effort paths
docs: add examples and migration guide for json_schema response_format
fix: handle edge case with empty streaming fragments causing premature validation
review_comments: Kenji Mori: Overall looks solid. Can we avoid buffering full output for large sequences? Suggest incremental structural checks and an upper bound to buffer size.
Marina Alvarez: Addressed: added incremental validation hooks that run on each top-level token and enforce a 64KB canonicalization buffer cap; added fail-fast errors when exceeded.
Priya Reddy: Please add an example for the OpenAI compatibility layer and document the exact mapping rules.
Marina Alvarez: Added compat mapping docs and tests; clarified naming of the json_schema field in the compat layer.
Alex Thompson: Tests look good. One nit: the error payload keys should be stable strings (code/string) for SDKs to parse easily.
Marina Alvarez: Normalized error payload to include "code", "message", "path", "suggested_fix". Updated SDKs to expose these fields as strings where appropriate.
release_notes: Added JSON Schema-based response_format with optional strict validation and structured validation errors. Streaming is supported; in strict mode streams terminate with an error if final output fails validation. Default non-strict behavior preserves backwards compatibility. SDK helpers added for Python and TypeScript.
